answer_1.quote: we design a three-stage pipeline: 1) Decomposition & Transformation that decomposes the graph into fragmented spans/sentences in natural language; 2) Grouping & Ordering that logically organizes the procedural fragments; 3) Aggregating & Smoothing that unifies the fragments into high-quality documents.

answer_2.quote: We adopt two commonly used Data2Text metrics. The FINE score models the evaluation as a natural language inference task - by inferring fragments from the documents it checks omissions, while the other direction checks hallucinations. The ESA score evaluates the coverage of entities and actions in the documents.

answer_4.quote: we ask three workers to score the document from 1 to 5 on five criteria: readability, the quality of the document to be understood easily; accuracy, the quality of the document accurately describing the information in the procedure graph; clarity, the quality of the document expressing the complex execution of actions logically; simplicity, the quality of the document not containing redundant information; usability, the quality of the document aiding users in accomplishing this procedure.
answer_4.guideline: we ask three workers to score the document from 1 to 5 on five criteria: readability, accuracy, clarity, simplicity, usability
